facts.fact: Amazon PPC advertising allows brands, agencies, and third-party sellers to target specific keywords for advertisements that appear in search results and competitor product listings.
facts.quote: target specific keywords to create advertisements for their products, which appear in Amazon's search results

facts.fact: Three out of four Amazon sellers of all types and sizes utilize Amazon PPC advertising.
facts.quote: three out of four Amazon sellers of all types and sizes utilize

facts.fact: ACoS is calculated by dividing total ad spend by attributed sales.
facts.quote: calculated by dividing total ad spend by attributed sales

facts.fact: Attributed sales are the total product sales generated within one week of clicks on ads.
facts.quote: total product sales generated within one week of clicks on your ads

facts.fact: Sales data can take up to 48 hours to populate and is not available in the Today date range.
facts.quote: sales data can take up to 48 hours to populate

facts.fact: Impressions represent the number of times ads were displayed and can take up to three days to remove invalid clicks.
facts.quote: number of times your ads were displayed

facts.fact: Clicks from the last three days may be adjusted due to click invalidation.
facts.quote: Clicks from the last three days may be adjusted due to click invalidation

facts.fact: When starting PPC campaigns, set daily budgets and default bids 50-100% higher than Amazon recommends.
facts.quote: set daily budgets and default bids 50-100% higher than what Amazon recommends

facts.fact: Let ad campaigns run for at least two weeks before running reports and making adjustments.
facts.quote: Let ad campaigns run for at least two weeks before running reports

facts.fact: Before adjusting or removing a keyword from a manual campaign, ensure the keyword gets at least 10 clicks.
facts.quote: make sure the keyword gets at least 10 clicks

facts.fact: 77% of Amazon SMB sellers use Sponsored Products ads.
facts.quote: 77% use Sponsored Products ads

facts.fact: 39% of Amazon SMB sellers use Sponsored Brands ads.
facts.quote: 39% use Sponsored Brands ads

facts.fact: 30% of Amazon SMB sellers use Sponsored Display ads.
facts.quote: 30% use Sponsored Display ads

facts.fact: Sponsored Products ads appear in search results and product listing pages and can closely resemble organic listings.
facts.quote: appear in search results and product listing pages, and can closely resemble organic listings

facts.fact: Sponsored Products is the most common type of Amazon PPC ad, used by 66% of third-party sellers.
facts.quote: most common type of Amazon PPC ad, used by 66% of third-party sellers

facts.fact: Automatic targeting involves Amazon's algorithm determining keywords related to product listings and adjusting ads based on shopper data.
facts.quote: targeting keywords that Amazon's algorithm determines are related to your product listing

facts.fact: Close match ads appear when shoppers use search terms closely related to the advertised product.
facts.quote: Appear when shoppers use search terms that are closely related to the product

facts.fact: Loose match ads appear when shoppers search keywords loosely related to the product.
facts.quote: Appear when shoppers search keywords loosely related to your product

facts.fact: Substitutes targeting reaches shoppers considering products similar to yours but sold by different brands.
facts.quote: Target shoppers who are considering products that are similar to your product but sold by a different brand

facts.fact: Complements targeting targets shoppers viewing detail pages of products that complement yours.
facts.quote: Target shoppers viewing detail pages of products that complement yours

facts.fact: Manual targeting involves hand-selecting keywords to bid on and only appears if search terms match chosen keywords.
facts.quote: hand-selecting the keywords you want to bid on

facts.fact: Sponsored Brands ads allow sellers to drive awareness to multiple products at once with robust visuals.
facts.quote: drive awareness to more than one product at a time and catch shoppers' eyes with more robust visuals

facts.fact: Sponsored Brands ads can appear at the top of search results as headline banners or as video further down the page.
facts.quote: appear either at the top of Amazon search results as headline banners or further down the page as a video

facts.fact: Sponsored Brands video format includes a 15-30 second-long video showcasing a single product.
facts.quote: includes a 15-30 second-long video showcasing a single product

facts.fact: Sponsored Brands ads navigate customers to custom landing pages or brand Amazon Storefronts.
facts.quote: navigate the customer to a custom landing page or a brand's Amazon Storefront

facts.fact: Sponsored Brands ads generate the most sales of all PPC types according to community data.
facts.quote: Sponsored Brand ads generates the most sales of all the PPC types

facts.fact: Products in the $21-$30 price range hit a sweet spot with greater RoAS than both more and less expensive products.
facts.quote: those in the $21-$30 price range hit a sweet spot, with a greater RoAS

facts.fact: Sponsored Display ads allow sellers to retarget customers who visited their product detail pages on and off Amazon.
facts.quote: retarget customers who have visited their product detail pages, on and off Amazon

facts.quote: appear on Amazon's affiliate sites, including Google, Facebook, Netflix, and even mobile phone apps

facts.fact: Sponsored Display ads require a registered brand to utilize them.
facts.quote: a seller must have a registered brand in order to utilize them

facts.quote: just 25% of third-party Amazon sellers use Sponsored Display PPC ads

facts.quote: making it easier for brands to create lifestyle imagery that helps improve their ads' performance with AI-powered image generation

facts.quote: click-through rates can be 40% higher compared to ads with standard product images

facts.quote: leftover amount can be used to increase ads by 10% on a later date in the same month

facts.fact: When starting out, set daily budget to $50 or more since most costs per click are between $0.50 to $1.50.
facts.quote: setting your daily budget to $50 or more. Most of your costs per click will be between $0.50 to $1.50

facts.fact: Ad costs are charged either when reaching $500 in total ads or at the first of the month.

facts.fact: Dynamic bids down only lowers bids in real-time when less likely to make a sale.
facts.quote: Amazon lowers bids in real-time when you're less likely to make a sale

facts.fact: Dynamic bids up and down can increase bids by 10% when ads are more likely to convert.
facts.quote: Amazon will increase the price of your bid by 10%

facts.fact: Fixed bids mean Amazon does not change the bid amount unless the seller adjusts it.
facts.quote: You set your bid and Amazon does not change it

facts.quote: Amazon suggests $0.75 to start, regardless of the product

facts.quote: bidding as high as $1.50 to $2.00 to ensure early sales

facts.quote: listing of the product must be eligible for the product listing's Buy Box

facts.quote: usually takes 30 minutes to an hour for your ad to premiere on Amazon

facts.fact: Poor-performing keywords are defined as those with more than 10 clicks and high ACoS or low 7-day conversion rate.
facts.quote: selecting keywords that have had more than 10 clicks, and a high ACoS or low 7-day conversion rate

facts.fact: If ACoS is less than profit margin, it is considered a good ACoS.
facts.quote: If your ACoS is less than the profit margin, then it is a good ACoS

facts.fact: Community practice aims for conversion rates of around 10% for products priced between $18-$25.
facts.quote: We aim for conversion rates of around 10% for products priced between $18-$25

facts.fact: High-performing keywords are defined as having at least 10 clicks and being at or below ACoS or conversion rate thresholds.
facts.quote: any keyword that has at least 10 clicks and is at or below your threshold for ACoS

facts.fact: High-performing keywords from automatic campaigns should be added to manual campaigns and removed from automatic targeting.
facts.quote: add those keywords to your existing manual-targeting sponsored product ads

facts.fact: Keyword research for manual targeting can be performed using related keyword searches or reverse ASIN lookups.
facts.quote: search using a related keyword. The second type is called a 'Reverse ASIN lookup'

facts.fact: Reverse ASIN lookup reveals keywords for which a competitor's product is ranking.
facts.quote: Keyword Scout reveals the keywords for which your competitor's product is ranking

facts.fact: 30-Day search volume exact is the number of times Amazon shoppers entered the exact term while performing searches.
facts.quote: number of times Amazon shoppers entered the exact term while performing a search

facts.fact: 30-Day trend is the increase in searches for a term over the last 30 days compared to the previous 30-day period.
facts.quote: increase in searches for a particular search term over the last 30 days

facts.fact: 30-Day search volume broad counts searches for terms closely related to the given search term.
facts.quote: number of times Amazon shoppers entered search terms closely related to the given search term

facts.fact: PPC bid exact represents the average bid current sellers use for sponsored products ads using exact keywords.
facts.quote: average bid current sellers are using to make their sponsored product ads appear using the exact keyword

facts.fact: PPC bid broad represents the average bid current sellers use for sponsored products ads using closely related keywords.
facts.quote: average bid current sellers are using to make their sponsored product ads appear using closely related keywords

facts.fact: HSA bids represent the average bid current sellers use for sponsored brand ads at the top of Amazon searches.
facts.quote: average bid current sellers are using to make their sponsored brand ads appear at the top of Amazon searches

facts.fact: Amazon's suggested bids tend to be somewhat conservative for new campaigns.
facts.quote: Amazon's suggested bids tend to be somewhat conservative

facts.fact: Community best practice is to review ad reports once per week.
facts.quote: Continue reviewing your ad reports once a week
